<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Beginning a systematic review of the PianoMode scripts to catalog files, identify performance bottlenecks, and trace the full gameplay data flow.

Several unused APIs and dead code were identified. HarmonyEngine.ValidarAcierto is only referenced in tests. PianoGameManager.StartGame is never called outside its own class. HasGameplayStarted and IsReadyToStartGameplay appear unused. ShowDetectedChord and the entire ChordDetectorUI system are unreachable from gameplay.

More dead code was found. HitLineRenderer is unused because StaffRenderer handles its own hit lines. Methods like GetActiveNotes, OnNoteRelease, ExitPreviewMode, ApplyVerticalScroll, ClearLedgerLines, SetHitLinePerfect, SetHitLineGood, SetHitLineColor, PulseHitLine, TriggerHitEffect, SongExists, GetRightHandMelody, GetTargetPublicScore, GetCurrentAudienceCap, and LogStatistics are unreachable or empty stubs. Fields such as beatOffsetTime and recorded_duration are unused. ResultsPanel.Hide is also dead code.

More performance and dead-code issues surfaced. ToggleLock is only a public wrapper with no internal usage. PlayerSpawnPoint and RecenterPlayer overlap functionally. PianoPublicSystem writes totalNoteCount, correctNoteCount, and lastWindowAverage without ever reading them back. GetCurrentSongTime is invoked both inside Update and on every MIDI event, and each call performs a GetComponent lookup that may return null. GetMidiNotes allocates a fresh array on every single call. MusicNote.Update polls IsNotePressedNow every frame for every active note. NoteSpawner.Update repeatedly fetches PianoGameManager.Instance via a static lookup each frame.

HarmonyEngineTests carry a RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod attribute, causing them to execute at AfterSceneLoad during production builds despite residing in the EditMode test folder.

DirectMidiReceiver polls JNI every millisecond. MIDIConnectionManager.Update runs every frame. ProgressDisplay.Update scans every active note each frame.

ControladorAudienciaPiano.Update repeatedly calls FindObjectOfType when sistemaPublico is null, and recaches animators via FindGameObjectsWithTag every two seconds.

Camera.main appears in the PianoCalibrator Update path. Shader.Find is used inside CreateLineCube. A new Material is instantiated for every ledger line.

Instantiate calls lack object pooling. FindExpectedGuideStaff allocates GetMidiNotes inside a loop. UpdateHitLineFeedback is dead code; it only resets the feedback timer instead of flashing the hit line. TriggerHitFeedback merely records the current time, so successful hits never trigger the green flash. This is a behavior bug where hits silently fail to display visual feedback.

Duplicate `MidiToNoteName` implementations exist across MusicNote, ProgressDisplay, ChordDetectorUI, and GameplayScoring.Diagnostics. Multiple classes maintain their own song time source—PianoGameManager.gameTime, GameplayScoring.GetCurrentSongTime, NoteSpawner.currentSongTime, MusicNote.GetCurrentSongTime, and ProgressDisplay.GetCurrentGameTime—creating redundant and inconsistent timing logic.

PianoPublicSystem.BuildAudienceComputationSnapshot is invoked twice per note event: once after CaptureCurrentPerformanceSample for logging, and again every Update cycle. It also recomputes the full snapshot after each UpdateLivePerformanceValues call.

GameplayScoring.Update redundantly calls SetApplauseVolume every frame, while PianoPublicSystem independently manages applause volume. Both systems update the same audio parameter.

PauseScoring correctly pauses held-duration accumulation because Update exits early when isGameActive is false, and MIDI events also respect that flag.

ResumeScoring does not reset lastProcessedTime, but this is harmless because audio pauses and the source time remains frozen.

MusicNote.GetCurrentSongTime contains a pause bug. When music is paused, the method falls back to Time.time minus fallbackStartTime. Because Time.time keeps advancing during pause, the song time drifts forward while playback is suspended.

GameplayScoring correctly uses source.time even when paused, since the audio source retains its position. MusicNote and NoteSpawner do not check isPlaying, so during pause they continue scrolling notes using unscaled Time.time. NoteSpawner.Update exits early when isSpawning is false, but MusicNote.Update still executes and advances note positions while playback is suspended. This creates a concurrency bug where notes drift forward during pause.

HarmonyEngineTests produce Debug.Log spam in player builds because they run at every scene load. UDPReceiver and SUDPReceiver usage needs verification. HitLineRenderer references in scenes must be checked. Unused field subscribers for OnNoteHit and OnNoteMissed need cleanup. Shader.Find costs require measurement. GetMidiNotes allocation needs closer inspection. PlayNote performs a linear nearest-sample search on every note-on event.

Checking for overlap between CantoMode ControladorAudiencia and PianoMode ControladorAudienciaPiano. Also verifying whether Pianoibrator.pianoSpawnPoint is unused.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Checking UDPReceiver usage across scenes.

DirectMidiReceiver polls every 0.001 seconds, causing 1000 JNI calls per second. NoteNames is duplicated four times. PianoCalibrator calls Camera.main every frame. MIDIConnectionManager runs Update each frame. Notes are instantiated and destroyed without pooling. GetMidiNotes allocates. Shader.Find appears in hot paths. ClearAllNotes uses FindObjectsOfType. Applause volume is duplicated. lastWindowAverage is unused. packetsReceived is only for logging.

GameplayScoring calls GetComponent inside GetCurrentSongTime, which Update invokes every frame. GetMidiNotes runs on every MIDI note-on through TrackOnsetTiming, FindExpectedGuideStaff, and ApplyVisualFeedbackToNoteStaffs. A nearest-note lookup could use binary search instead of linear scan. AccumulateHeldDurationForMidiNote uses heldDurations.ContainsKey rather than allocating.

`new[] { note.GetMidiNote() }` allocates even when the array is empty. `Array.IndexOf` on `GetMidiNotes` runs inside loops. `MusicNote` carries unused `rightHandColor` and `leftHandColor` fields. `enableHarmonyAnalysisDebugLogs` and `enableAudienceSyncLogs` both default to true, forcing constant GC pressure in production. `ReportVisualFeedbackLatency` always calls `Debug.Log` with no toggle. `MIDIStatusReceiver` and `HarmonyEngineTests` still need review for edit-mode versus runtime behavior.

DirectMidiReceiver’s 0.001-second check interval is misleading because Update runs roughly once per frame, so the receiver polls every frame anyway. maxEventsPerFrame is fixed at 256 in Start, and each event triggers a JNI dequeueEvent call. MidiAudioManager.Update safely dequeues from a ConcurrentQueue, which is the correct thread-safe handoff.

DirectMidiReceiver enqueues events on the main thread via JNI polling, while its consumer also runs on the main thread. Using a ConcurrentQueue for MIDI is therefore unnecessary. UDPReceiver appears to be a legacy background-thread MIDI path; it may be unused for piano input, whereas SUDPReceiver is actively used by CantoMode for singing pitch.
</details></think>

# PianoMode audit — `Assets/Scripts/PianoMode/`

Read all **32** `.cs` files, plus `HarmonyEngine.cs`, `HarmonyEngineTests.cs`, and the MIDI/UDP path they depend on (`DirectMidiReceiver`, `MIDIConnectionManager`, `MIDIStatusReceiver`, `UDPReceiver`).

---

## 1. Full file list

### Managers

## 2. Performance issues

### Update() doing heavy / redundant work

**`ProgressDisplay.Update`** rebuilds rich-text **and scans every `all_notes` entry** every frame:

```47:48:c:\Users\vic-s\Desktop\etheriavr_metaquest3\Assets\Scripts\PianoMode\UI\ProgressDisplay.cs

    void Update() => UpdateDisplay();
```

```138:151:c:\Users\vic-s\Desktop\etheriavr_metaquest3\Assets\Scripts\PianoMode\UI\ProgressDisplay.cs
    private void CollectCurrentTrebleNotes()
    {
        currentTrebleNotes.Clear();
        // ...
        foreach (GameNoteData note in gameManager.currentSongData.all_notes)
        {
            if (note.clef != "treble") continue;
            if (currentGameTime >= note.time && currentGameTime < note.time + note.duration)
                currentTrebleNotes.Add(note);
        }
    }
```

**`ControladorAudienciaPiano.Update`** calls `FindObjectOfType` / `Camera.main` every frame, and **re-FindGameObjectsWithTag("Publico") every 2s** (also re-rolls random offsets):

```39:44:c:\Users\vic-s\Desktop\etheriavr_metaquest3\Assets\Scripts\PianoMode\Gameplay\ControladorAudienciaPiano.cs
    {
        ResolveDependencies();
        if (listaAnimadores.Count == 0 || Time.unscaledTime >= siguienteRecacheo)
            CacheAudienceAnimators();
```

**`MusicNote.Update`** (one per visible note) polls song time + `IsNotePressedNow` every frame. No pooling; N notes = N Updates.

**`GameplayScoring.Update`** every frame: hold accumulation, **applause volume**, miss scan, dead hit-feedback timer.

**`PianoGameManager.Update`** polls `FindObjectOfType<MIDIConnectionManager>` / `PianoPauseMenu` every 0.5s until found.

**`MidiAudioManager.Update`** drains the MIDI queue (necessary) then optionally logs.

**`HitLineRenderer.Update`** (two instances in `PianoGame.unity`) writes `material.color` + emission every frame.

**`PianoCalibrator.Update`** is fine for calibration, but calls `Camera.main` repeatedly for hint/label orientation.

**`ChordDetectorUI.Update`** fades alpha even though nothing ever shows a chord.

### Allocations (new List, string concat, LINQ)

|---|---|
| `GameplayScoring.GetMidiNotes` | `new[] { note.GetMidiNote() }` on fallback, called from MIDI onsets and staff search |

| `PianoPublicSystem.LogAudienceSync` | string concat + `new[]` in `FormatMidiNotes` on every match/wrong note (default **true**) |
| `GameplayScoring.ReportVisualFeedbackLatency` | **unconditional** `Debug.Log` with `$"..."` on every burn segment |
| `MusicNote.GetActiveNotes` | `new List` + `FindObjectsOfType` (unused, but toxic if ever called) |
| `NoteSpawner.ClearAllNotes` | `FindObjectsOfType<MusicNote>()` |
| `ProgressDisplay` | TMP string every frame (StringBuilder helps; still dirtying UI mesh) |

`GetMidiNotes` hot allocation:


### FindObjectOfType / GetComponent / GameObject.Find

**Per spawned note** (worst spawn-time hitch):


**Every Update until resolved:** `ControladorAudienciaPiano.ResolveDependencies`, `PianoGameManager.TryAttachMidiConnectionManager`.

**Start-time scene-wide scans:** `Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll<PianoGameManager>()` and **all Transforms** in `FindSceneObjectByName("EndGameUI")`. `MidiAudioManager.ResolveApplauseClip` walks every `MidiAudioManager`, `ControladorAudiencia`, then **every `AudioSource`**.

**GetComponent in hot-ish paths:** `StaffRenderer.HitLineRenderer => hitLine.GetComponent<Renderer>()` on every flash; `GameplayScoring.GetCurrentSongTime` can `GetComponent<PianoGameManager>()` if null (once). Not in Update after cache, except audience recache.

**Camera.main** in `PianoCalibrator.GetLookTargetPosition` / hint transform every calibration frame; `ControladorAudienciaPiano` if `jugador` is null.

### Debug.Log on hot paths

Default-on:

- `enableHarmonyAnalysisDebugLogs = true` → log per NoteOn + per finalize
- `enableAudienceSyncLogs = true` → log per live match / wrong note / evaluated note
- `ReportVisualFeedbackLatency` → **always** logs, no flag

MIDI verbose is off by default (good). `HarmonyEngineTests` dumps 9 logs on first scene load in **player builds**.

### Coroutines that poll

None busy-wait. Countdown / fade / hit-flash use `WaitForSeconds` (OK). `ResultsPanel.FadeIn` yields null for 0.5s (OK).

- `ControladorAudienciaPiano`: `FindGameObjectsWithTag("Publico")` on a timer
- `FindSceneObjectByName` iterates every Transform in memory

### Extra Quest-relevant costs

- `MidiAudioManager.Start` forces **poolSize ≥ 128** `AudioSource`s on one GO
- `Shader.Find` + `new Material` per duration line, burn segment, ledger line
- `Instantiate`/`Destroy` notes with no pool; `CreatePrimitive(Cube)` per line

## 4. Duplicate / overlapping systems

1. **Song clock (5 copies):** `PianoGameManager.gameTime`, `GameplayScoring.GetCurrentSongTime`, `NoteSpawner` audio.time, `MusicNote.GetCurrentSongTime`, `ProgressDisplay.GetCurrentGameTime`. Scoring uses `source.time` even when paused; **MusicNote requires `isPlaying`**, so notes **keep scrolling during pause**.
2. **Hit line:** `StaffRenderer` cube vs `HitLineRenderer` (two scene instances) vs unused `SetHitLinePerfect/Good`.
3. **Audience:** `PianoPublicSystem` ≈ copy of `SingPublicSystem`; `ControladorAudienciaPiano` ≈ `ControladorAudienciaSing`; leftover `ControladorAudiencia` disabled at runtime. Applause volume set in **both** `GameplayScoring.Update` and `ResumeAudienceApplause`.
4. **MIDI ingest:** `DirectMidiReceiver` (JNI, used) vs `UDPReceiver` on `PianoGame.unity` (thread + socket, **unused queue**).
5. **Player placement:** `PlayerSpawnPoint` vs `RecenterPlayer` vs calibrator spawn point.
6. **MIDI note names:** four copies of `NoteNames` + `MidiToNoteName` (`MusicNote`, `ProgressDisplay`, `ChordDetectorUI`, `GameplayScoring.Diagnostics`).
7. **Staff assignment:** `NoteSpawner` midi≥60 vs `GameNoteData.clef` (ProgressDisplay uses clef; spawn ignores it).
8. **Song formats:** `all_notes` vs legacy `melody`/`chords`.
9. **Connection polling:** `DirectMidiReceiver` + `MIDIStatusReceiver` (0.5s) + `MIDIConnectionManager.Update` every frame + `PianoGameManager` lookup.
10. **Duplicate PianoGameManager** adoption via `Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll` — papering over scene duplicates.

---

`[AudienceSync] event=LiveWindowMatched midi=[60,64,67] onTime=True public=12.0%->18.4%`

`[FeedbackLatency] midi=60 isCorrect=True deltaMs=...` — **every burn segment, uncapped**.

## 6. Data flow (current vs tighter, same behavior)

```
SelectedSongManager.file_path
        │
        ▼
PianoSongLoader (JSON + MP3)
        │
        ▼
PianoGameManager.OnSongLoaded
  ├─ Apply DB metadata
  ├─ GameplayScoring.InitializeForSong (sort, per-note score maps)
  └─ NoteSpawner.LoadSong (flatten midi_notes → PianoNoteData) + preview
        │
PianoCalibrator.OnPianoConfigured → Countdown 3-2-1-GO
        │
MIDI gate (MIDIConnectionManager / DirectMidiReceiver)
        │
        ▼
Same frame: AudioSource.Play + StartScoring + StartSpawning
        │
JNI poll (DirectMidiReceiver.Update)
  → ConcurrentQueue<byte[3]>
  → MidiAudioManager.ProcessMidi (synth + events)
        │
        ├─ GameplayScoring.ProcessMidiNoteOn
        │     TrackOnsetTiming → live audience pulse / wrong-note penalty
        │     live staff spheres
        ├─ MusicNote.Update: move by song time; burn if IsNotePressedNow
        └─ GameplayScoring.Update: hold overlap, DetectMissedNotes → FinalizeExpectedNote
                    │
                    ▼
           PianoPublicSystem window (5.25s) → applause volume
           ControladorAudienciaPiano → Animator "Calidad"
                    │
song time ≥ GetGameDuration()
        │
CalculateFinalScore → ResultsPanel → SavePracticeSession → Repertorio
```

**Same-behavior, cheaper flow:**

1. **One `ISongClock`** (`AudioSource.time` if clip exists, else `Time.time - start`). Inject into scoring, spawner, notes, HUD. Pause = freeze clock (`time` while paused), so notes stop.
2. **Wire refs in the inspector / once in `PianoGameManager.Start`.** Pass `MidiAudioManager` + `GameplayScoring` into `MusicNote.Initialize`. Ban `FindObjectOfType` after `Start`.
3. **Event-driven burn:** NoteOn/Off for that MIDI id, not per-note `IsNotePressedNow` polling.
4. **Object pool** for `MusicNote` + reuse duration/burn meshes; cache Unlit material.
5. **Score from a cursor** (`nextExpectedNoteIndex`) already exists — reuse it in `ProgressDisplay` instead of full-list scan.
6. **One applause writer:** `PianoPublicSystem` publishes score; `MidiAudioManager` samples it (not scoring **and** manager).
7. **Logs off by default**; compile-out diagnostics (`#if UNITY_EDITOR` or a single `PianoDebug` flag).
8. Keep flatten-at-load; don’t re-derive hand/staff per spawn beyond a precomputed staff enum.

---

## 7. Threading / concurrency

| Path | Threads | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| `DirectMidiReceiver` | **Main only.** JNI `dequeueEvent` in `Update`, enqueue `byte[3]` | `ConcurrentQueue` is unnecessary here (same thread as `MidiAudioManager`). Allocates a new 3-byte array per event. |
| Java `MidiInputBridge` | Native MIDI callback thread inside the plugin | Correctly polled on main; don’t call Unity APIs from Java. |
| `UDPReceiver` | **Background `Thread` + `UdpClient(12345)`** | Present on `PianoGame.unity`. Queue is **never consumed** → **unbounded growth** if anything sends UDP. `Debug.Log` from the worker on bind failure. `OnApplicationQuit` Join(5s) can stall quit. |
| `currentlyPressedNotes` / `activeNotes` | Main thread only | Safe today. |
| `MIDIConnectionManager.Update` | Main | Polls connection every frame; can start an HTTP coroutine on connect. |
| `HarmonyEngineTests` | Main, first scene load | Extra logs; not a race. |

No Unity API is called from the UDP worker except `Debug.LogError` in `catch` (unsafe). Piano MIDI does not need that thread.

`checkInterval = 0.001f` does **not** poll at 1 kHz; `Update` is once per frame (~72 Hz on Quest). The tooltip is misleading.

## HarmonyEngine + tests

`HarmonyEngine` is small and correct: perfect window → 1, quadratic falloff to scoring window, `ValidarAcierto` is pitch+window AND.

Tests cover offsets 0 / 0.02 / 0.04 / 0.14 / 0.24 and three `ValidarAcierto` cases. Gaps: `scoringWindow < perfectWindow`, negative offset (API takes absolute), `ValidarAcierto` unused in production so a scoring regression wouldn’t fail these tests.

**Problem:** folder says EditMode, but they are **runtime logs**, not `[Test]` / NUnit. They run in Quest builds once per app session.

---

## Refactor recommendations (by impact)

1. **Kill default-on logs** (`harmony`, `audience`, `FeedbackLatency`). Biggest GC + logcat win; zero gameplay change. Rank: **critical**.
2. **Inject `MidiAudioManager` / `GameplayScoring` at spawn**; stop per-note `FindObjectOfType`. Rank: **critical** (Quest hitch when many notes spawn).
3. **Single song clock**; use `audio.time` while paused so notes freeze. Rank: **high** (fixes pause drift; also removes 5 clocks).
4. **Disable/remove `UDPReceiver` from `PianoGame`**. Rank: **high** (thread, port, unbounded queue).
5. **Note object pool + shared Unlit material**; cache `Renderer` on hit line. Rank: **high**.
6. **`ProgressDisplay`**: cursor into sorted notes, or 10 Hz refresh. Rank: **high**.
7. **Cache audience animators once**; never `FindObjectOfType` in `Update`. Rank: **high**.
8. **Convert `HarmonyEngineTests` to real EditMode NUnit**; strip `RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod`. Rank: **medium-high**.
9. **Precompute MIDI→sample table (21–108)**; don’t linear-search the sample list. Rank: **medium**.
10. **One applause volume owner**; drop duplicate `SetApplauseVolume` from scoring `Update`. Rank: **medium**.
11. **Wire scene refs**; delete `FindSceneObjectByName` / `AdoptConfiguredReferencesFromScene` once duplicates are gone. Rank: **medium**.
12. **Delete or park dead APIs:** `ChordDetectorUI` path, unused staff flash methods, empty `LogStatistics` / `OnNoteRelease`, unused song split getters, `ValidarAcierto` if scoring won’t use it. Rank: **medium** (clarity).
13. **Event-driven burn** instead of polling `IsNotePressedNow`. Rank: **medium**.
14. **`GetMidiNotes` without allocating**; store `midi_notes` always. Rank: **low-medium**.
15. **Either use `HitLineRenderer` or StaffRenderer, not both**; call `SetHitLinePerfect` on hits or remove `staffHitFeedbackTime`. Rank: **low** (visual consistency).
16. **Lower default voice pool** (e.g. 32–48) unless polyphony needs 128. Rank: **low-medium** (Start cost).
17. **Unify MidiToNoteName** in one helper. Rank: **low**.

I would do 1–4 first: they cut Quest frame spikes and allocations without changing scoring math.
